### Getting started with FastAPI 0.159.1

Path: `/sourcey-docs-fastapi/docs/getting-started/`

# Getting started with FastAPI 0.159.1 {#getting-started-with-fastapi-01591}


Everything below is taken from the pinned upstream tree at
[`ce6ee83e5411`](https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/tree/ce6ee83e5411b98582e996e47edf7870418a68f4).


## Install {#install}


```bash
pip install fastapi
```


## The smallest application {#the-smallest-application}


```python
from fastapi import FastAPI

app = FastAPI()


@app.get("/")
async def read_root():
    return {"message": "Hello World"}
```

`FastAPI` is exported from `fastapi.applications` and re-exported at the package
root. Its constructor accepts 37 arguments —
every one of them is listed on the [configuration](https://asporeteam.github.io/sourcey-docs-fastapi/docs/reference/config/index.md) page.


## The router {#the-router}


```python
from fastapi import APIRouter

router = APIRouter(prefix="/items", tags=["items"])


@router.get("/{item_id}")
async def read_item(item_id: int):
    return {"item_id": item_id}


app.include_router(router)
```


## Path operation decorators {#path-operation-decorators}


`FastAPI` and `APIRouter` both expose the same family of path-operation
decorators — 16
HTTP verbs plus `api_route` and `websocket_route`. See [routing](https://asporeteam.github.io/sourcey-docs-fastapi/docs/reference/routing/index.md).


## Request parameters {#request-parameters}


```python
from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, HTTPException

app = FastAPI()


def common_params(q: str | None = None, skip: int = 0):
    return {"q": q, "skip": skip}


@app.get("/items/")
async def read_items(commons: dict = Depends(common_params)):
    return commons
```


## Interactive docs {#interactive-docs}


`FastAPI` serves the OpenAPI UI at `/docs` (Swagger UI) and `/redoc` by default;
both paths are constructor arguments and can be turned off.

| `get` | `get(path: Annotated[str, Doc('\n                The URL path to be used for this *path operation*.\n\n                For example, in `http://example.com/items`, the path is `/items`.\n                ')], *, response_model: Annotated[Any, Doc("\n                The type to use for the response.\n\n                It could be any valid Pydantic *field* type. So, it doesn't have to\n                be a Pydantic model, it could be other things, like a `list`, `dict`,\n                etc.\n\n                It will be used for:\n\n                * Documentation: the generated OpenAPI (and the UI at `/docs`) will\n                    show it as the response (JSON Schema).\n                * Serialization: you could return an arbitrary object and the\n                    `response_model` would be used to serialize that object into the\n                    corresponding JSON.\n                * Filtering: the JSON sent to the client will only contain the data\n                    (fields) defined in the `response_model`. If you returned an object\n                    that contains an attribute `password` but the `response_model` does\n                    not include that field, the JSON sent to the client would not have\n                    that `password`.\n                * Validation: whatever you return will be serialized with the\n                    `response_model`, converting any data as necessary to generate the\n                    corresponding JSON. But if the data in the object returned is not\n                    valid, that would mean a violation of the contract with the client,\n                    so it's an error from the API developer. So, FastAPI will raise an\n                    error and return a 500 error code (Internal Server Error).\n\n                Read more about it in the\n                [FastAPI docs for Response Model](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/response-model/).\n                ")]=Default(None), status_code: Annotated[int | None, Doc('\n                The default status code to be used for the    ')]=None, response_model_by_alias: Annotated[bool, Doc('\n                Configuration passed to Pydantic to define if the response model\n                should be serialized by alias when an alias is used.\n\n                Read more about it in the\n                [FastAPI docs for Response Model - Return Type](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/response-model/#response_model_include-and-response_model_exclude).\n                ')]=True, response_model_exclude_unset: Annotated[bool, Doc('\n                Configuration passed to Pydantic to define if the response data\n                should have all the fields, including the ones that were not set and\n                have their default values. ### Routing

Path: `/sourcey-docs-fastapi/docs/reference/routing/`

# Routing {#routing}


`FastAPI` and `APIRouter` share the same routing API. Every HTTP verb is a
decorator that registers a path operation.

| Method | On | Signature | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `openapi` | FastAPI | `openapi() -> dict[str, Any]` | Generate the OpenAPI schema of the application. This is called by FastAPI |
| `setup` | FastAPI | `setup() -> None` | — |
| `add_api_route` | FastAPI | `add_api_route(path: str, endpoint: Callable[..., Any], *, response_model: Any=Default(None), status_code: int \| None=None, tags: list[str \| Enum] \| None=None, dependencies: Sequence[Depends] \| None=None, summary: str \| None=None, description: str \| None=None, response_description: str='Successful Response', responses: dict[int \| str, dict[str, Any]] \| None=None, deprecated: bool \| None=None, methods: list[str] \| None=None, operation_id: str \| None=None, response_model_include: IncEx \| None=None, response_model_exclude: IncEx \| None=None, response_model_by_alias: bool=True, response_model_exclude_unset: bool=False, response_model_exclude_defaults: bool=False, response_model_exclude_none: bool=False, include_in_schema: bool=True, response_class: type[Response] \| DefaultPlaceholder=Default(JSONResponse), name: str \| None=None, openapi_extra: dict[str, Any] \| None=None, generate_unique_id_function: Callable[[routing.APIRoute], str]=Default(generate_unique_id)) -> None` | — |
| `api_route` | FastAPI | `api_route(path: str, *, response_model: Any=Default(None), status_code: int \| None=None, tags: list[str \| Enum] \| None=None, dependencies: Sequence[Depends] \| None=None, summary: str \| None=None, description: str \| None=None, response_description: str='Successful Response', responses: dict[int \| str, dict[str, Any]] \| None=None, deprecated: bool \| None=None, methods: list[str] \| None=None, operation_id: str \| None=None, response_model_include: IncEx \| None=None, response_model_exclude: IncEx \| None=None, response_model_by_alias: bool=True, response_model_exclude_unset: bool=False, response_model_exclude_defaults: bool=False, response_model_exclude_none: bool=False, include_in_schema: bool=True, response_class: type[Response]=Default(JSONResponse), name: str \| None=None, openapi_extra: dict[str, Any] \| None=None, generate_unique_id_function: Callable[[routing.APIRoute], str]=Default(generate_unique_id)) -> Callable[[DecoratedCallable], DecoratedCallable]` | — |
| `add_api_websocket_route` | FastAPI | `add_api_websocket_route(path: str, endpoint: Callable[..., Any], name: str \| None=None, *, dependencies: Sequence[Depends] \| None=None) -> None` | — |

               ```python\n                from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI\n\n                from .dependencies import get_token_header\n                from .internal import admin\n\n                app = FastAPI()\n\n                app.include_router(\n                    admin.router,\n                    dependencies=[Depends(get_token_header)],\n                )\n                ```\n | `add_event_handler` | APIRouter | `add_event_handler(event_type: str, func: Callable[[], Any]) -> None` | Add an event handler function for startup or shutdown. |
| `on_event` | APIRouter | `on_event(event_type: Annotated[str, Doc('\n                The type of event. `startup` or `shutdown`.\n                ')]) -> Callable[[DecoratedCallable], DecoratedCallable]` | Add an event handler for the router. |


## Minimal example {#minimal-example}


```python
from fastapi import FastAPI

app = FastAPI()


@app.get("/items/")
async def read_items():
    return [{"id": 1}]


@app.post("/items/")
async def create_item(payload: dict):
    return {"id": 2, **payload}
```


## Path parameters and path converters {#path-parameters-and-path-converters}


```python
@app.get("/items/{item_id}")
async def read_item(item_id: int):
    return {"item_id": item_id}
```


## Routers {#routers}


```python
from fastapi import APIRouter

router = APIRouter()


@router.get("/health")
async def health():
    return {"ok": True}


app.include_router(router, prefix="/api", tags=["meta"])
```


## WebSockets {#websockets}


```python
from fastapi import WebSocket


@app.websocket("/ws")
async def ws(websocket: WebSocket):
    await websocket.accept()
    await websocket.send_json({"hello": "world"})
    await websocket.close()
```


## Middleware and events {#middleware-and-events}


`add_middleware`, `middleware`, `on_event`, `add_event_handler` and
`exception_handler` are available on both the application and the router.

         function* ends, but **before** the response is sent back to the client.\n                So, the dependency function will be executed **around** the *path operation\n ## Using them {#using-them}


```python
from typing import Annotated

from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, Query

app = FastAPI()


def api_key_header(x_key: Annotated[str, Query()]):
    return x_key


@app.get("/items/")
async def read_items(
    q: Annotated[str | None, Query(max_length=50)] = None,
    x_key: Annotated[str, Depends(api_key_header)] = "",
):
    return {"q": q, "x_key": x_key}
```

Every helper above is defined in `fastapi.param_functions` and is re-exported
from the package root, so `from fastapi import Depends, Query` is the public path.


### Responses

Path: `/sourcey-docs-fastapi/docs/reference/responses/`

# Responses {#responses}


FastAPI returns a `Response` subclass automatically when a path operation
returns a `Response` instance directly, or when `response_model` is not used.

| Class | Summary |
|---|---|
| `UJSONResponse` | JSON response using the ujson library to serialize data to JSON. |
| `ORJSONResponse` | JSON response using the orjson library to serialize data to JSON. |
| `FileResponse` | re-exported from starlette.responses |
| `HTMLResponse` | re-exported from starlette.responses |
| `JSONResponse` | re-exported from starlette.responses |
| `PlainTextResponse` | re-exported from starlette.responses |
| `RedirectResponse` | re-exported from starlette.responses |
| `Response` | re-exported from starlette.responses |
| `StreamingResponse` | re-exported from starlette.responses |


## Returning a response directly {#returning-a-response-directly}


```python
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse


@app.get("/raw")
async def raw():
    return JSONResponse({"ok": True}, status_code=201)
```


## Media types {#media-types}


`HTMLResponse`, `PlainTextResponse`, `StreamingResponse`, `FileResponse` and
`RedirectResponse` cover the common cases; the `responses` module also exposes
the `ORJSONResponse` and `UJSONResponse` fast serialisers.


### Exceptions

Path: `/sourcey-docs-fastapi/docs/reference/exceptions/`

# Exceptions {#exceptions}


| Class | Module | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| `EndpointContext` | fastapi.exceptions | — |
| `HTTPException` | fastapi.exceptions | An HTTP exception you can raise in your own code to show errors to the client. |
| `WebSocketException` | fastapi.exceptions | A WebSocket exception you can raise in your own code to show errors to the client. |
| `FastAPIError` | fastapi.exceptions | A generic, FastAPI-specific error. |
| `DependencyScopeError` | fastapi.exceptions | A dependency declared that it depends on another dependency with an invalid |
| `ValidationException` | fastapi.exceptions | — |
| `RequestValidationError` | fastapi.exceptions | — |
| `WebSocketRequestValidationError` | fastapi.exceptions | — |
| `ResponseValidationError` | fastapi.exceptions | — |
| `PydanticV1NotSupportedError` | fastapi.exceptions | A pydantic.v1 model is used, which is no longer supported. |
| `FastAPIDeprecationWarning` | fastapi.exceptions | A custom deprecation warning as DeprecationWarning is ignored |


## Raising an HTTP error {#raising-an-http-error}


```python
from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException

app = FastAPI()


@app.get("/items/{item_id}")
async def read_item(item_id: int):
    if item_id < 0:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Item not found")
    return {"item_id": item_id}
```


## Custom exception handlers {#custom-exception-handlers}


```python
@app.exception_handler(HTTPException)
async def http_exception_handler(request, exc):
    return JSONResponse({"detail": exc.detail}, status_code=exc.status_code)
```

## Common configuration {#common-configuration}


```python
from fastapi import FastAPI

app = FastAPI(
    title="My API",
    version="1.0.0",
    description="A FastAPI application.",
    docs_url="/docs",
    redoc_url="/redoc",
    openapi_url="/openapi.json",
)
```

## How the inventory was produced {#how-the-inventory-was-produced}


The generator parses the pinned tree with Python's `ast` module — the package
is never imported, so no dependency has to be installed to produce the
inventory. For every module it records the public classes, their public
methods and the public functions, each with a rendered signature and the first
line of its docstring. The upstream documentation tree under `docs/en/docs/` is
copied verbatim.
